name: The Quarry's Smith

angles.text: As a blacksmith, you can learn from Frast Dokner, a field mentor for apprentice smiths. He trades his hard-won forging techniques to anyone who supplies the raw metal and leather that keep his anvil hot.
As a miner working the surrounding deposits, you have a buyer close at hand for your smelted copper bars. They go toward practical training and camp repairs.
As a dwarf, you can see Bronzebeard industry at Gol'Bolar Quarry, where dwarven resolve keeps the forges burning when supply caravans run late.
As an Alliance member, you can help keep the remote dwarven quarry running and its equipment ready in the snowy high country.

faq.answer: Frast Dokner is an experienced blacksmith at a quarry encampment. He maintains tools, structural fittings, and equipment for the workers there. When delays cut off his regular supply line, he asks passing travelers to gather the raw materials he needs.

aliases: why copper bars and boar hides
faq.answer: Quarry work and camp upkeep use great amounts of sturdy materials. Copper is an accessible, workable metal for replacement fittings, nails, fasteners, and bands that reinforce broken tools. Boar hides provide tough leather for bellows, tool wraps, straps, and protective aprons against sparks and the grinding work.
faq.q: Why does the quarry need copper bars and boar hides?

faq.answer: Frast Dokner does not explain why the shipment is late. Overland routes across snowy crags and mountain passes often face blizzards, roaming wildlife, and hostile trogg or bandit ambushes. Remote mining camps and quarries feel the strain first when transport wagons fall behind.
faq.q: Why is the supply shipment late?

faq.answer: Frast Dokner offers more than coin: he promises to share his personal blacksmithing techniques with whoever gathers the needed supplies. An aspiring artisan can learn practical metalworking and equipment care from a seasoned field craftsman, lessons city guildhalls rarely teach novices.
faq.q: What does Frast Dokner offer in exchange for the materials?

faq.answer: Frast Dokner works at Gol'Bolar Quarry in Dun Morogh, south of Kharanos. The dwarven excavation lies in snowy foothills and faces harsh winter weather and aggressive subterranean troggs, who harass miners and disrupt trade convoys from Ironforge.

aliases: is the quarry part of ironforge
faq.answer: Frast Dokner and the quarry camp are under the Bronzebeard clan and the Kingdom of Ironforge. Quarrying stone and mining ore in Dun Morogh support the kingdom's construction projects and defenses. Blacksmiths such as Dokner help sustain Ironforge's industry.
faq.q: Is Frast Dokner affiliated with Ironforge?

sections.body:
An excavation needs steady care. Pickaxes must be sharpened, worn brackets replaced, and camp gear reinforced. When a vital shipment misses its schedule, work begins to grind to a halt. Without fresh stock from the major trade routes, the craftsmen must improvise and look to passing travelers for help.

Frast Dokner works the forge through these delays. He asks anyone willing to gather basic metals and hides to help keep the camp running, rather than wait for transport wagons that may be far behind.
sections.title: Shortages at the Quarry

sections.body:
Dwarven blacksmithing guilds prize discipline and guard their methods, rarely sharing trade secrets with casual wanderers. Dokner weighs that custom against the camp's immediate needs. He lacks workable copper and durable leather for patching tools and camp gear.

Bring the raw materials to his anvil, and he will teach you his personal smithing techniques. The bargain trades useful craft knowledge for materials the camp needs to endure and keep its gear in repair.
sections.title: An Apprentice's Bargain

summary: At the quarry, The Quarry's Smith, Frast Dokner, needs metal and leather for camp repairs. With a supply shipment late, he asks travelers to bring the materials. In return, Dokner offers practical smithing techniques.
